description: Prototype alert rules (assumptions, not utility policy). Edit this file to change behavior.

short.reason: Low risk and a short expected outage.

medium.reason: Low risk and an outage of several hours.

long.reason: Low risk and a day or longer expected outage.

extended.reason: Low risk and a multi-day expected outage.

unknown.reason: Low risk and no restoration estimate.

short.reason: Moderate risk and a short expected outage.

medium.reason: Moderate risk and an outage of several hours.

long.reason: Moderate risk and a day or longer expected outage.

extended.reason: Moderate risk and a multi-day expected outage.

unknown.reason: Moderate risk and no restoration estimate.

short.reason: Higher risk and a short expected outage.

medium.reason: Higher risk and an outage of several hours.

long.reason: Higher risk and a day or longer expected outage.

extended.reason: Higher risk and a multi-day expected outage.

unknown.reason: Higher risk and no restoration estimate.
We could not rate the risk for this location, so we use a cautious general level.

N1.reason: A need you declared raises the alert level one step.

N2.reason: A declared medical-equipment need sets the alert level to at least elevated.

N3.reason: A declared medical-equipment need with an outage of several hours (or no reliable rating) sets the highest level.

info.reason: Basic level: outage and restoration alerts, storm alerts only if you opt in.

standard.reason: Standard level: storm alert the day before and again closer to the storm.

elevated.reason: Elevated level: earlier and more frequent alerts.

priority.reason: Priority level: earliest alerts, fastest updates, voice first.

K-pre.reason: Your alert level qualifies you for storm alerts.

K-pre-unrated.reason: We can't rate your risk, so we send a general storm alert to be safe.

K-pre-optin.reason_opted_in: Your alert level is basic, and you opted in to storm alerts.
K-pre-optin.reason_not_opted_in: Your area is rated lower for this scenario. You can still opt in to storm alerts.

K-out.reason: Every enrolled customer is alerted when an outage is confirmed.

K-upd.reason_changed: The estimate moved enough to be worth telling you about.
K-upd.reason_small: The estimate has not changed enough to send another message.
K-upd.reason_recent: We sent an update recently, so we wait before sending another.
K-upd.reason_no_prior: You get an update when the estimate changes by a meaningful amount.

K-restored.reason: Every enrolled customer is told when power is restored.

E1.reason: The typical estimate is a day or longer, so a person should follow up.

E2.reason: A declared medical-equipment need plus an outage of several hours (or no reliable estimate) calls for priority outreach.

E3.reason: The high end of the range reaches several days, so share shelter and resource information.

E4.reason: The estimate range is very wide, in both relative and absolute terms, so a person should review it before it is shared.

E5.reason: You declared a need and the typical estimate is a day or longer, so resource outreach is recommended.

assumptions: These alert rules are prototype assumptions, not utility policy.
Needs are only the ones you declared. We do not guess them.
Escalations are recommendations for a person to act on, not automatic actions.
The alert level is a prototype level for this demo, not a service commitment.
